# Dossier — Why is the sky blue? (fixture)

Sunlight contains the full visible spectrum. Air molecules (N₂, O₂) are far smaller than the wavelength of
visible light, so they scatter light in the Rayleigh regime, where scattered intensity scales as 1/λ⁴.
Blue light (~450 nm) is therefore scattered roughly (700/450)⁴ ≈ 5.9 times more than red light (~700 nm).
Scattered light reaches the observer from all directions of the sky, so the sky appears blue.
(Fixture text; a real dossier is far longer and cites every paragraph.)
